answer: Duplicate or cloned identifiers are rejected at the registration ledge, and any attempt to spin up many identities requires acquiring and bonding separate hardware tokens at real cost. Each agent must stake a unique hardware-backed pearl token, registered on-chain with a signed plume identifier tied to its physical device. Attackers thus face steep per-identity capital outlays, making mass sybil creation economically unviable while honest agents keep low entry friction. In practice, Agent0144 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
